prompt:
Build the VMware Cloud Foundation architecture deliverable in this repository. The design target is VCF 9.0.0.0 and the stated capacity, availability, site, hardware, and network inputs are in `requirements/greenfield-requirements.json`. The brownfield comparison inventory is in `fixtures/estate-inventory.json`.

Before implementing the design, use your network research tools to consult current, real, reachable Broadcom-published compatibility and interoperability material for the supported software/hardware combinations and the VCF 5.x-to-9.0 upgrade path. Record what you actually consulted in `research/consulted-sources.json` as a nonempty JSON array of objects. Each object must contain a nonempty string `title`, an absolute Broadcom- or VMware-published HTTP(S) string `url`, a nonempty string `retrievedAt`, and an `informedDecisions` array with one or more nonempty strings. Do not treat the local compatibility fixture as a substitute for this live research. Live sources may have changed; `fixtures/compatibility-snapshot.json` is the pinned authority for the deterministic deliverable.

Implement `src/VcfArchitecture/VcfArchitecture.psm1` as a PowerShell module. `New-VcfArchitecture` must accept `-RequirementsPath`, `-InventoryPath`, `-CompatibilitySnapshotPath`, and `-OutputPath`, consume those three input documents, and write `artifacts/vcf-architecture.json`. Give the artifact `artifactVersion` `1.0`. Under `greenfield`, put the input identity in `requirementsId`; copy the four stated capacity values into `capacity`; put `objective`, `selectedArchitecture`, `hostCount`, `minimumPhysicalNicGbps`, and `alternatives` in `storageDecision`; and put `topology`, `maximumInterSiteRttMs`, `dataSites`, and `witness` in `siteTopology`. Each alternative must contain `architecture`, `hostCount`, `dataHostsPerSite`, `minimumPhysicalNicGbps`, and `mtu`; each data-site placement must contain `siteId`, `faultDomain`, and `hostnames`; the witness must contain `siteId`, `faultDomain`, and `hostname`. Compare the supported vSAN OSA and ESA choices, select the option required by the stated selection objective, and carry the resulting host count, equal two-site host placement, minimum physical uplink speed, MTU, VLANs, and storage settings into the architecture.

The artifact's `greenfield.sddcSpec` must be a VCF Installer `SddcSpec` valid against `specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json`, pinned from tag `9.0.0.0` of `vmware/vcf-api-specs`, and must carry the applicable SDDC, host, DNS, NTP, cluster, network, uplink, and vSAN values from the inputs. Do not put live credentials in it. Represent every populated password as a deployment-time placeholder in the form `${UPPER_SNAKE_CASE_NAME}`.

The artifact must also contain `existingEstate.migrationPlan`, valid against `schemas/migration-plan.schema.json`. Include exactly one ordered step for every component in the supplied inventory, naming its current version, pinned target, action, and all of its compatibility gates. Represent the OSA-to-ESA transition using the supported migration mode fixed by the snapshot.

Wire the module to the installed `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Installer` prerequisite rather than vendoring any VMware module. Export both `New-VcfArchitecture` and `Invoke-VcfArchitectureInstallerValidation`. The validation command must turn the generated JSON into VMware SDK model objects with the applicable `Initialize-VcfInstaller*` commands and submit the typed spec with `Invoke-VcfInstallerValidateSddcSpec`. Do not invoke installer validation while generating the deliverables. The completed work is the module, generated architecture JSON, and consulted-source record, not a prose architecture report. Run `pwsh -NoLogo -NoProfile -File tests/verify.ps1` to check the deliverable.
